commit.message:
tests: migrate supplied legacy sources at their own position; record legacy hook-table digests

Address review on #309 (f5830dd):
- installation_tests() now falls back to legacy identification for any
  v7-marked source that is not the current helper (as the installer does), so
  the runner can execute against the accepted pre-release v7 identities. A
  supplied legacy install of any identity is migrated and compared against
  apply_v7(clean, at=<its helper position>) and re-applied as a no-op, instead
  of being compared with the fresh-install bytes; with adaptive-K between the
  two positions that comparison was wrong. The same position rule is covered
  with the public v5-main fixture, helper before and after adaptive-K.
- legacy_scheduler_helpers.py records HOOK_TABLE_DIGESTS for the V1/V2/V5/V6
  hook tables. They are checked unconditionally (no scheduler source needed,
  also as a plain pytest test), so a changed table is caught on build-shaped
  and deployed sources too, where the whole-source digests cannot apply. A
  wrong begin_step hook in the V5 or V6 table now fails on every source layout.

Tests only; the installed scheduler on image ef9f5013 is still sha256
97c90a18fd0df6f9aeb1452c39801455d90756d315c6846ca0642e934fe4e269.

scheduler: refuse import drift on legacy installs; ship the migration fixture in the image; record legacy digests

Address review on #309 (b852f57):
- _identify() refuses a legacy install whose `import os` is missing
  ("import drifted") instead of repairing it during migration, matching
  the check the current-v7 path already had. Three refusal cases added; the
  refusal test now also requires a deliberate refusal message, not a crash.
- Dockerfile: the fixtures COPY now ships tests/fixtures/legacy_scheduler_helpers.py
  to /opt/glm53/fixtures/, and the runner resolves its fixture beside itself
  before the checkout tree, so the mandatory build-time self-test
  (python3 /opt/glm53/test_scheduler_decode_floor.py) finds it. New
  tests/test_image_test_layout.py stages the Dockerfile's /opt/glm53 layout
  from its COPY lines and checks that resolution (and, with
  GLM53_SCHEDULER_PY_SRC set, runs the full runner there).
- legacy_scheduler_helpers.py records PINNED_CLEAN_SHA256 and a SOURCE_DIGESTS
  entry per reconstructed legacy install on the pinned source. On that source
  the installation test compares each rebuild against its recorded digest and
  checks the comparison's sensitivity, so the installer's hook tables are
  checked against recorded history rather than against themselves. A wrong
  begin_step hook in the V5 or V6 table is now caught.

Installer-only change: the installed scheduler on image ef9f5013 is still
sha256 97c90a18fd0df6f9aeb1452c39801455d90756d315c6846ca0642e934fe4e269.

tests: consolidate decode-floor producer fixtures into legacy_scheduler_helpers.py

Replace the six vendored copies of older patcher scripts under
tests/fixtures/decode_floor_producers/ with the byte-exact helper texts of
the same identities (v1-image-d9758a6, v5-main, v5-priority,
v6-warm-deadline, v6-carry), appended to tests/fixtures/legacy_scheduler_helpers.py
in the format #180 established for v1/v2/v5-historical, with provenance in
its docstring.

installation_tests() rebuilds every accepted public identity the same way:
helper text at the installer's anchor plus that version's hook pairs. Each
rebuild was checked byte-identical to the output of the removed patcher
copy, and the installer still authenticates each by sha256 and length.
v5-historical is now exercised directly as well. Same coverage (9 of 11),
about 3,600 fewer lines, no new file layout.

scheduler: refuse unknown markers and duplicate wrappers; test deployed v7 at its own position

Address independent verification of #309 at 7340644:
- _identify() treats a source as pristine only when no decode-floor marker
  of any version and no helper name (_Glm53MixedPrefill, _GLM53_MIXED,
  _glm53_mixed_prefill_policy) is present; an unknown marker such as
  "# [glm53-decode-floor:v99]" is refused without writing instead of being
  installed beside.
- _unpatch() applies the same rule to whatever remains after removing the
  identified install, so a later duplicate policy wrapper (which would
  rebind the global the hooks call) no longer verifies as current.
- installation_tests() compares a deployed v7 against apply_v7() at the
  helper's own position, so a scheduler that also carries adaptive-K (the
  deployed layout, helper before _Glm53AdaptiveK) passes; both compositions
  are checked explicitly. New refusal cases: duplicate wrapper on v7 and on
  pristine, unknown marker, unknown text after the helper.

Installer-only change: on image ef9f5013 the installed scheduler is still
sha256 97c90a18fd0df6f9aeb1452c39801455d90756d315c6846ca0642e934fe4e269
and re-applying on the deployed layout verifies without writing. The two
unpublished v7 pre-release identities still migrate to the fresh-install
bytes.

scheduler: refuse leftover decode-floor markers after unpatch; canary rejects any URL userinfo

Address review on #309:
- _unpatch() now refuses when any decode-floor marker (any version) or
  either helper definition remains after removing the identified install.
  A canonical v7 with a stray v5 or v1 marker no longer verifies as
  "already present". Installer-only change: on image ef9f5013 the
  installed scheduler is still sha256
  97c90a18fd0df6f9aeb1452c39801455d90756d315c6846ca0642e934fe4e269.
- check_concurrent_agents.py rejects password-only and empty-user userinfo
  (e.g. http://:secret@host), not only a non-empty username.
- Regressions: v7-plus-v5/v1-marker refusals in installation_tests() and
  tests/test_check_concurrent_agents.py; both fail on the previous code.

tests: cover v7 re-verification, native KV refusal recovery, all public producers

Address review on #309:
- installation_tests() verifies an already-current v7 scheduler exactly (as
  the patcher's main() does) before unpatching, then checks it equals a fresh
  install and that re-applying is a verified no-op.
- New multi-step regression: a selected waiter natively refused KV lets the
  runnable peer progress in the same step, is not preselected for one step,
  stays a candidate and recovers once memory frees, while the peer keeps
  progressing (#246). Fails if the refusal is ignored or the refused waiter
  keeps its slot.
- Byte-exact producer fixtures for every accepted public identity:
  v1-image-d9758a6 (helper rebuilds image ef9f5013 byte-for-byte),
  v5-historical (e329e55), v6-warm-deadline (#180, f89e240) and v6-carry
  (#246, dc702b4), each migrated and re-applied.

docs: decode-floor v7 references; drop stale concurrent-agents page (#283)

REFERENCE.md: name decode-floor v7 where it said v5, and describe the v7
installer contract (v3/v4 and drifted installs are refused, not migrated).
Drop docs/concurrent-agents.md from this integration: its launcher-default
statements predate main's fair default on all launchers.

scheduler: integrate #246, #221 and #180 as decode-floor v7 (#283)

Replace the fair-prefill decode-floor overlay with the integrated v7 patcher
qualified in #283:

- a selected WAITING request refused KV allocation no longer stalls a
  runnable prefill; it keeps being retried and recovers once memory frees (#246)
- explicit priorities keep ranking fair-prefill candidates under
  --scheduling-policy priority; FCFS is unchanged (#221)
- installer migration follows #180's fail-closed contract: pristine, v1, v2,
  v5 and v5+priority installs migrate to the fresh-install v7 bytes; v3/v4,
  drifted, duplicated, marker-only and unmarked helpers are refused unwritten

patch_mamba_align_chunking.py accepts decode-floor v7. #180's concurrency
canary, its docs and its CPU progress regressions land with it. The
decode-floor installation test is ported to the v7 contract with deployed
producer fixtures, and the mamba A4 fixture downgrades v7 as well as v5.

On image ef9f5013 these overlays install scheduler sha256
97c90a18fd0df6f9aeb1452c39801455d90756d315c6846ca0642e934fe4e269, the
identity qualified live in #283 (baseline -> candidate -> baseline, TP2).

the worker. Count the pinned base's 32 layers plus the Dockerfile's
COPY/RUN/ADD steps (skipping heredoc bodies and continuations) and cap at
123, the largest depth observed to load. The counter reproduces the measured
123-layer image at 6227eea and fails on b356b2c (126).

commit.message:
fix(tp3,tp4): caller export of GLM53_DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT wins over .env

.env.example ships an empty GLM53_DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT= line, so sourcing
.env silently replaced a caller export on start-tp3.sh (#299) and
start-tp4.sh. Capture it setness-aware before .env and restore it after
.env.tpX, like GLM53_INDEXER_WORKSPACE and start.sh. test_start_overrides
covers caller > .env.tpX > .env on both launchers; it fails without the
capture.
